name: Tetouan
hero_subtitle: White Andalusian medina under the Rif — crafts, museums and the Mediterranean nearby.

overview.title: Tetouan: White Medina, Place Hassan II and the Road to the Sea
overview.p1: Tetouan is the white city of Andalusian memory: monumental gates, vast granaries and a medina that is easier to walk than Fez. Place Hassan II sets the scene; the kasbah shows the scale of the old stronghold. It is also the natural base for Martil and Chefchaouen without the day-trip rush from farther cities.
overview.p2: Two full days cover the imperial core and the medina; a third day fits the coastal town of Martil or the Rif mountains. Stays cluster near the medina and Ville Nouvelle — practical if you want both history and calm evenings.

eat.title: Where to Eat in Tetouan
eat.subtitle: Square terraces, medina grills and reliable Ville Nouvelle tables.

placehedim.title: Cafés on Place Hassan II
placehedim.desc: Mint tea and simple meals with Place Hassan II in view — best at golden hour when the gate lights up.

medina_grill.title: Medina grills & olive stalls
medina_grill.desc: Skewers, bread and olives where locals eat. Follow busy tables rather than empty tourist boards.

riad_restaurant.title: Riad courtyard restaurants
riad_restaurant.desc: Set menus in restored houses a few minutes from the square — book for a quiet dinner.

ville_nouvelle.title: Ville Nouvelle cafés & brasseries
ville_nouvelle.desc: Coffee, pastries and easier seating after a day on your feet near the train station side of town.

rooftop.title: Rooftop viewpoints
rooftop.desc: A few rooftops near the walls for sunset over the imperial city — ask your riad for the current best table.

local_tagine.title: Tagine & couscous houses
local_tagine.desc: Slow-cooked standards. Ask for the day’s pot rather than a fixed tourist menu only.

transport.title: Getting around without wasting time
transport.desc: The medina and Place Hassan II are walkable. Use petits taxis for Martil or the kasbah heights. Agree the price before you start or insist on the meter.

bargain.title: Shopping and expectations
bargain.desc: Souks are calmer than Fez. Polite bargaining is normal for crafts. Museum tickets and official sites have fixed prices.

water.title: Heat, water and timing
water.desc: Summer afternoons are hot in the lanes. Do the medina and kasbah in the morning, carry water, and keep Martil or museums for later.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Tetouan
daytrips.subtitle: Easy excursions that fit comfortably into a single day.

volubilis_combo.title: Chefchaouen day trip
volubilis_combo.desc: The blue town in the Rif — a classic full day from Tetouan by shared taxi or organised tour.

fes.title: Tangier
fes.desc: About an hour by road — medina, cafes and the Strait when you want a busier coastal day.

rabat.title: Ceuta border / Fnideq
rabat.desc: Shopping and border energy north of town — only if paperwork and timing suit you.

azrou.title: Martil & the coast
azrou.desc: Mediterranean beach time a short taxi ride away — ideal late afternoon after the medina.

q1.question: How many days should I spend in Tetouan?
q1.answer: Two full days cover the main sights comfortably. Three or four days allow a relaxed pace plus a day trip to Chefchaouen or Tangier.

q2.question: Is Tetouan safe for tourists?
q2.answer: Yes. Like any large city, use normal precautions. Tourist areas, the beach and the centre are generally well-frequented and feel safe.

q3.question: What currency is used and can I pay by card?
q3.answer: Morocco uses the dirham (MAD). Cards are widely accepted in hotels and restaurants; keep some cash for taxis, markets and smaller shops.

q4.question: How do I get to Tetouan from Tangier or the airport?
q4.answer: Grand taxis and private transfers connect Tangier to Tetouan in about an hour. Tetouan also has Sania Ramel airport for regional flights.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A relaxed schedule to see the highlights without rushing.

detailed_itinerary.day1_m: Morning — Place Hassan II & medina edge
detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start on Place Hassan II while the light is soft, then enter the white medina lanes for crafts and everyday life.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Climb toward the kasbah walls for views over the roofs, then return through quieter residential streets.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Dine near the square or in the ville nouvelle — Tetouan evenings are calmer than Tangier.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Visit the Archaeological Museum for Roman and local finds, then walk toward the Royal Palace facade (exterior only).
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: See the Modern Art Museum, then explore the Mellah quieter fabric before the heat peaks.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: A calm dinner in the centre; keep the night early if you leave for Martil tomorrow.
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Artisan quarter or free time
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Return to a favourite medina corner or the artisan lanes without a fixed checklist.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Taxi to Martil for Mediterranean air, a walk on the sand and simple seafood.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: A final stroll on Place Hassan II before continuing toward Tangier, Chefchaouen or the coast.
